newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-VELEZ BEAT EIGHT-MAN CRUZEIRO TO WIN SUPERCUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VELEZ BEAT EIGHT-MAN CRUZEIRO TO WIN SUPERCUP.

text.p: Argentina's Velez Sarsfield won the South American Supercup on Wednesday after comfortably winning the second leg of the final against Brazilians Cruzeiro, who had three players sent off.

Velez, who also had a player dismissed, won 2-0 to take the tie 3-0 on aggregate and add another cup to their bulging trophy cabinet. Cruzeiro, knocked out in the quarter-finals of the Brazilian championship at the weekend, were left to lament another near miss.

Velez goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert missed out on a chance to finish as the tournament's joint top-scorer when he had a penalty saved by his opposite number Dida late in the game. He had already scored three Supercup goals this year, two from penalties and one from a free kick.
The contest was as good as over after ten minutes by which time Velez, already 1-0 up from the match in Brazil, had scored twice.

The smoke from the fireworks which greeted the teams' arrival was still clearing when Patricio Camps fired the first goal from close range in the fourth minute after being left alone by the Cruzeiro defence at a free kick.
Four minutes later, Cruzeiro's hopes of winning the trophy for the third time evaporated when defender Gelson slid the ball into his own goal as he tried to clear a low cross by Camps.
After that Velez appeared happy to stroke the ball around the field, encouraged by cries of "ole" from an ecstatic home crowd.
With nothing to play for apart from their pride, Cruzeiro, who committed an average of 29 fouls a match in the Brazilian championship, lost their heads in the second half.

Left-back Nonato was the first to go after throwing himself feet-first at the shins of an opponent. Shortly afterwards he was joined in the dressing room by team-mate Fabinho, who was sent off for clashing with Velez captain Mauricio Pelligrino, who was also dismissed.
Then, Cruzeiro substitute Donizete was sent off less than five minutes after coming on as a substitute for another wild challenge.

Velez had little tradition until they won the first Argentine championship of the 1993/4 season. They followed this by winning the South American Libertadores Cup in 1994 and beat Italy's Milan to win the Intercontinental Cup the same season.
They also won both the championships of the 1995/6 Argentine season.
The club, from the Buenos Aires suburb of Liniers, have been hugely influenced by the extrovert Chilavert.
In addition to his goalkeeping ability, the Paraguayan international regulary scores goals from free kicks and penalties and is an expert at psyching out opposing players.

Velez Sarsfield - 1-Jose Luis Chilavert, 4-Flavio Zandona (14-Sebastian Mendes, 81st minute), 2-Victor Hugo Sotomayor, 6- Mauricio Pellegrino, 3-Raul Cardozo, 17-Guillermo Moriggi, 18- Claudio Husain, 5-Marcelo Gomez, 7-Christian Bassedas, 11- Martin Posse (9-Fernando Pandolfi, 77th), 10-Patricio Camps (20- Omar Assad, 74th).
